lessons.situation: A maintenance request was on hold after the tenant completed the agency's troubleshooting checks, and the landlord had already agreed in advance to an engineer attending if the fault persisted. The tenant then replied that the fault was still present.
lessons.action: When a tenant reports that troubleshooting has not fixed the fault and the landlord has already pre-approved an engineer visit, do not ask the landlord again. Confirm internally that the issue is unresolved, assign the maintenance provider, tell the tenant the provider will contact them to arrange a visit or quote, send the provider the job details with an instruction to quote and wait for approval if needed, and then return the request to auto mode.
lessons.rationale: The tenant's reply meets the condition the landlord already approved, so the job can go straight to provider assignment without delay or a duplicate approval request, and the tenant and provider both get clear next steps.

lessons.situation: A tenant reports an appliance fault, the agency suggests a troubleshooting setting from the manual, and the tenant replies that the appliance has still never worked and asks for someone to inspect it.
lessons.action: When the tenant says self-help troubleshooting has failed and asks for an inspection, send a short holding reply to the tenant saying you will be back in touch. Then email the landlord asking for approval to send an appliance repair contractor to inspect, and put the job on hold awaiting the landlord's response.
lessons.rationale: Once troubleshooting is ruled out, a contractor visit needs landlord approval, and the tenant should know it is being handled without being promised a visit before that approval.

lessons.situation: The landlord has approved the agency instructing a contractor for a minor plumbing repair, and the agency has assigned a provider and sent notifications to the tenant and the contractor, after which the system prompts a check on whether any response to the provider is needed.
lessons.action: After the landlord approves instructing a contractor, assign the maintenance provider, email the tenant with the provider name and what to expect, and send the contractor the job details, tenant contact and quote-approval conditions. Then check whether the provider needs any further reply; if the instruction already covers everything, return the request to auto mode rather than sending more messages.
lessons.rationale: The instruction email to the contractor already contains the contact details, scope and approval conditions, so no extra response is needed and the case can safely resume automated handling until the provider replies.

lessons.situation: After landlord approval and provider assignment on a plumbing request, the landlord sent only a brief acknowledgement that needed no reply, and the system prompted the operator to decide whether a response was needed or to return the job to auto mode.
lessons.action: Read the landlord's message to confirm it is only an acknowledgement with no question or instruction, so no reply is needed. Then switch the job back to auto mode so the automated provider chasing continues, and watch for the provider confirming a tenant appointment.
lessons.rationale: Replying to a simple thanks adds noise, while returning the job to auto mode lets reminders and follow-ups resume, which keeps the request moving toward booking.

lessons.situation: The agency needed a tenant's solar panel meter reading photo for a periodic landlord record, held the task until the due period, chased the tenant by email and phone, and the tenant eventually replied with the photo attached.
lessons.action: When the tenant's reply arrives with the requested meter reading photo, forward the attachment straight to the landlord, state which period the reading covers, and ask when they will next need one. Then mark the task complete without escalating or handing off to anyone else.
lessons.rationale: The task is a simple evidence-collection loop, so once the tenant supplies the photo the quickest way to close it is to pass it to the landlord with a note on the period and the next due date.

Subject: Approval needed – washing machine inspection, Flat 29, 19 Copperfield Walk, Northbridge, ZZ9 1ZZ (Ref R/PM039-1 / NBL-039-2915)

Dear Landlord,

The tenant has reported that the washing machine at Flat 29, 19 Copperfield Walk is making a mechanical clicking noise while the drum rotates during washes. The machine is still working at the moment. We asked the tenant to check that nothing inside the drum was hitting the sides, and she has confirmed the noise is mechanical. She has offered to send a video.

We would like to send an appliance repair engineer to inspect the machine and tell us the cause and the cost of repair. We don't have a cost estimate yet. If the engineer finds repair work is needed, we will send you their quote for approval before any work goes ahead.

Please reply APPROVE to let us arrange the inspection, or DECLINE if you would prefer to deal with it another way (for example, using your own engineer).

Kind regards,
Donna
Maintenance team

Thank you for checking the machine. Yes, please send the video by replying to this email. It will help the engineer.
